words.gloss: basti (enema); mishap, complication; siddhi: success, accomplishment, i.e. the successful treatment of the mishaps of basti

hindi: अब इसके बाद हम बस्ति की व्यापत्तियों यानी गड़बड़ियों की सिद्धि का व्याख्यान करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the siddhi (success, accomplishment) of the mishaps of basti (enema): the Bastivyāpatsiddhi.
notes: Chapter-opening formula. Title read as basti-vyāpatti-siddhi, "the accomplishment (successful treatment) of the mishaps of basti". The word siddhi is kept; "successful treatment" is an interpretive gloss.

words.gloss: vibandha: obstruction, retention (binding up); gaurava: heaviness; ādhmāna: distension, bloating; śiraḥ-ruj: head-pain (headache); vāhana: carrying, conveying (sense obscure here); ūrdhva-ga: going upward

hindi: विबन्ध यानी रुकावट, भारीपन, आध्मान यानी पेट का फूलना, सिर की पीड़ा, वाहन और ऊपर की ओर जाने वाले।
english: Vibandha (obstruction, retention), heaviness, ādhmāna (distension), head-pain, vāhana, and (ones) going upward.
notes: GROUPING: units 2, 3 and 4 read as one statement: 2 and 3 are lists, and 4 gives the cause (non-application and over-application of basti); no verb in 2 or 3. The list in 2 has six members as read here. "vāhana" (lit. "carrying, conveying") is obscure as a complication name; it may be a shortened form (for example pravāhaṇa, "straining"), but this is only a guess and is not applied; the printed word is kept. "ūrdhvaga" is taken as a list member, "(one) going upward" (compare unit 37, where the wind goes upward). Modern equivalents: vibandha = constipation or retention of stool/wind (probable); ādhmāna = abdominal distension, bloating (standard); śiroruj = headache (standard).

words.gloss: kukṣi: belly; śūla: pain, colic; aṅga: limb, body; ruci: liking, taste (sense of aṅga-ruci obscure); dhmā: blowing, puffing (a bare stem; doubtful here); hṛd: heart; pīḍā: pain, pressure; kartana: cutting (cutting pain); srava: flow, discharge

hindi: पेट की शूल, अंग-रुचि, ध्मा, हृदय की पीड़ा, कर्तन और स्राव।
english: Belly-colic (kukṣiśūla), aṅga-ruci, dhmā, heart-pain, cutting pain (kartana) and flow (srava).
notes: GROUPING: continues the list of 2; the statement is completed in 4. Members as read: kukṣiśūla, aṅgaruci, dhmā, hṛtpīḍā, kartana, srava (six). The printed "aṅgaruci" and "dhmā" are obscure: aṅga-ruci literally "liking of the body/limbs", possibly a mis-print of a pain-word or of aruci (distaste for food), and "dhmā" is a bare stem (√dhmā "blow") that may be a truncated form of ādhmāna or dhmāna; none of these readings is applied, the printed forms are kept and translated literally. The words are not corrected in the text_flags because no single correction is sure. Modern equivalents: kukṣiśūla = colicky belly pain (standard); kartana = cutting pain (standard).

hindi: बस्ति के अयोग यानी प्रयोग न होने से और अतियोग यानी अधिक प्रयोग से छह और छह आपत्तियाँ होती हैं।
english: From non-application (ayoga) and from over-application (atiyoga) of the basti (enema) there are six and six mishaps.
notes: Sandhi: ṣaṭṣaḍāpadaḥ = ṣaṭ ṣaṭ āpadaḥ ("six, six"). Read with 2 and 3. Whether the six of 2 are those of non-application and the six of 3 those of over-application is not stated in the text and is not assumed here. "ayoga/atiyoga" are kept literally as non- and over-application.

words.gloss: not oiled; sweated; of the body: of one whose body is not oiled and sweated (see notes)
heavy; koṣṭha (storehouse, belly); of one whose koṣṭha is heavy

hindi: जिसका शरीर स्निग्ध और स्वेदित नहीं है और जिसका कोष्ठ भारी है, उसमें प्रयुक्त।
english: Applied to one whose body is not oiled and not sweated, and whose koṣṭha (storehouse, belly) is heavy.

text_flags.why: possible: stray anusvara; "aṃsnigdha" is not a word, "asnigdha" (not oily) fits the sense and metre

notes: Elliptical: the noun "basti" is supplied only in 7; no noun is added in the translation. The negative a- is taken to govern both snigdha and svinna ("neither oiled nor sweated"), the natural sense; the alternative "not oiled, but sweated" is grammatically possible but less likely. The print has a stray anusvara in "aṃsnigdha". The sentence continues through 6 into 7 (verb in 8: karoti).

words.gloss: cold; little; sneha (oil, fat); salt; drug, substance; quantity

hindi: ठंडा, या जिसमें स्नेह, लवण, द्रव्य और मात्रा अल्प हो, अथवा गाढ़ा भी।
english: Cold, or with little oil, salt, drug and quantity, or even thick.

text_flags.why: possible: "olpa" for "alpa" (orthographic habit of this print, also in unit 27)

notes: Continues 5 (the noun basti is supplied only in 7). The print writes "olpa" for "alpa" (śīta + alpa would give śītālpa); read as alpa, and the same print habit recurs in 27 ("yuktolpavīryo"), recorded here once. Ambiguity: whether alpa ("little") applies to all four of sneha, lavaṇa, dravya, mātrā, and whether "cold" is a separate member, is not fixed by the compound; the plain reading is taken.

words.gram: pres. part. a-nir-√hṛ, m. nom. sg.

hindi: बस्ति उस दोष को क्षुब्ध करके, दुर्बलता के कारण उसे बाहर न निकालती हुई।
english: The basti, having agitated that doṣa and not expelling it because of weakness,
notes: The sentence continues in 8 (verb karoti). The subject of the weakness (durbalatva) is not stated; the natural reading is the basti, but it may be the patient. "durbalatvādanirharan" is printed as one word.

words.gloss: wind (vāta, flatus); stool; urine; obstruction, retention

hindi: वायु, मल और मूत्र का अत्यन्त भयंकर विबन्ध यानी रुकावट करती है।
english: Causes an extremely severe obstruction (vibandha) of wind (vāta), stool and urine.
notes: Completes 5-7. "vāta" is read here as passing wind (flatus), the natural sense in the series wind, stool, urine; the Vāta humour is not meant to be excluded but the plain sense is taken. Modern equivalent: vibandha = constipation or retention (probable).

words.gloss: basti (bladder, lower belly); navel; pain; ānāha (distension of the belly with retention)
heart; smearing, coating: hṛllepa (a "smearing" of the heart)

hindi: बस्ति और नाभि में पीड़ा, आनाह, हृदय का लेप और गुदा में सूजन।
english: Pain in the basti (bladder, lower belly) and navel, ānāha (distension of the belly), hṛllepa (a "smearing" of the heart), and swelling in the anus.
notes: Elliptical: the verb karoti of 8 is carried over, none is supplied. "basti" in the first compound is the organ (bladder, lower belly) not the enema,. Modern equivalents: ānāha = abdominal distension with obstruction (standard); hṛllepa = a coating or clinging sensation at the heart (probable); śvayathu = swelling (standard).

hindi: खुजली, गण्ड यानी गाँठें या सूजन, रंग का बिगड़ना, बेचैनी और अग्नि की मृदुता।
english: Itching, gaṇḍa (lumps, swellings), discolouration, restlessness (arati) and softness (mārdava) of the fire (vahni).

text_flags.why: orthographic variant (nh for hn); normalised in words

notes: Elliptical: the verb karoti of 8 is carried over, none is supplied. "vanhi" is the print's spelling of vahni (normalised, recorded here once). "gaṇḍa" has several senses (boil, swelling, also cheek); "lump, swelling" is taken. "vahni" is a name of the fire (agni); "softness of the fire" is kept literal, and probably points to weak digestion but this is not stated in the text.

hindi: पहले बताए गए दो काढ़े, मध्यम दोष में, अतिसार यानी दस्त वाले में।
english: The pair of decoctions prescribed earlier, in a middling doṣa, in one with atisāra (diarrhoea).

text_flags.why: possible: kvātha (decoction) with the v dropped; sense fits

notes: GROUPING: 11 and 12 form one statement (11 names the pair, 12 says which one is drunk). "kāthadvayam" is read as kvātha-dvaya (the pair of decoctions): the print drops the v. "prāgvihita" refers to decoctions prescribed earlier in the book; which ones is not stated here. "atisārin" is read as the adjective "one having atisāra" (diarrhoea, standard). The pair is not identified.

hindi: इसलिए वहाँ एक, उष्ण का, पीना प्रशंसित है।
english: Therefore, in that case the drinking of one, the hot one, is recommended.
notes: GROUPING: continues 11. "tasmāt" is read as "therefore", with "ekasya" "of one" (of the two decoctions); the alternative "of that one" is possible. "uṣṇa" ("hot") is the choice made between the pair; whether the heat is of temperature or of potency is not stated. No noun is supplied in the translation.

hindi: फलवर्तियाँ, वैसे ही स्वेद, समय को जानकर विरेचन।
english: Phalavartis (suppositories), likewise sweatings (sveda), and, having known the time, purgation (virecana).
notes: Elliptical list; no verb in the unit and none is supplied. "phalavarti" is kept as the Sanskrit term (lit. "fruit-wick"); a medicated suppository is the standard sense. Which time is meant is not stated.

words.gloss: trivṛt (turpeth, Operculina turpethum; standard); dāru (probably devadāru, deodar, Cedrus deodara; probable); yava (barley, Hordeum vulgare; standard); kola (jujube, Ziziphus jujuba; probable); kulattha (horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum; standard); having

hindi: बिल्व यानी बेल की जड़, त्रिवृत् यानी निशोथ, दारु यानी सम्भवतः देवदारु, यव, कोल यानी सम्भवतः बेर और कुलत्थ यानी कुलथी वाला।
english: Having bilva-root (wood-apple), trivṛt (turpeth), dāru (probably devadāru), yava (barley), kola (probably jujube) and kulattha (horse gram).
notes: GROUPING: 14 and 15 form one statement; "-vān" ("having") here qualifies the basti named in 15. Identifications: bilva = Aegle marmelos (standard); trivṛt = Operculina turpethum (standard); dāru = devadāru, Cedrus deodara (probable; "dāru" alone is wood and is not secure); yava = barley, Hordeum vulgare (standard); kola = jujube fruit, Ziziphus jujuba (probable); kulattha = horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum (standard). Whether "bilvamūla" belongs inside the long compound (the print has a space) is not fixed.

words.gloss: surā (a fermented liquor); beginning with; urine; having

hindi: सुरा आदि और मूत्र वाली बस्ति, बिगड़े शब्द के अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, उसे लाए।
english: The basti having surā and the others and urine, on a conjectural reading of the damaged word saprākūpeṣyaḥ, should bring it.
notes: The word "saprākūpeṣyas" is damaged or unintelligible in the print; no reading is built on it; the sense of the unit is therefore uncertain. "tam ānayet": the object tam and what is "brought" is not stated; what is "brought" is not stated. "surādi" is read as "surā etc." (the series beginning with surā), kept literal.

hindi: संशेष आम में, मृदु निरूह द्वारा, दोषों से प्रेरित।
english: In saṃśeṣa-āma (remaining āma), by a mild nirūha (decoction enema), stirred by the doṣas,
notes: GROUPING: continues in 17 (verbs mūrcchayati, ruṇaddhi, hinasti). The reading of "saṃśeṣāme" is uncertain: saṃśeṣa-āma "remaining āma (undigested matter)" is taken, which is not secure; the subject of "īritaḥ" is taken to be the basti (nominative masculine) but is not named. The construction is elliptical.

hindi: वायु को मूर्च्छित करता है, मार्ग को रोकता है और अग्नि को हानि पहुँचाता है।
english: It stupefies (mūrcchayati) the wind (anila), obstructs the path, and harms the fire (agni).
notes: Continues 16 (subject not stated; "it" is the basti). "mūrcchayati" (lit. "makes swoon", also "thickens, congeals") is rendered "stupefies". The "path" and the "fire" are kept literal; the text does not say which path.

words.gloss: heaviness; fatigue; heart; pain; burning; bewilderment; veṣṭana: enveloping, twisting pain

hindi: भारीपन, थकान, हृदय में शूल, दाह, मोह और ऐंठन।
english: Heaviness, fatigue, pain in the heart, burning, bewilderment and twisting (veṣṭana).
notes: GROUPING: continues 16-17 as the list of effects (verb carried over from the previous unit, none supplied). Modern equivalents: klama = fatigue, exhaustion (standard); saṃmoha = confusion, bewilderment (standard); veṣṭana = cramping, twisting pain (probable).

words.gloss: drying, rough; sweating; digestive, promoting digestion (pācana)

hindi: तब करे; उसका रूक्ष, स्वेदन और पाचन उपायों से उपचार करे।
english: Then one should do; one should treat him with drying (rūkṣa), sweating (sveda) and digestive (pācana) (ones).
notes: The verb "kuryāt" is left without an object; it is redundant beside "upacaret" and may be a mis-print or a remnant of another reading, but this is only a guess and is not applied. The instrumentals are neuter plural but no noun is stated.

words.gloss: pippalī (long pepper, Piper longum; standard); kattṛṇa (a grass; identity disputed, sometimes the scented grass rauhiṣa, Cymbopogon; disputed); uśīra (vetiver, Vetiveria zizanioides; standard); dāru (probably devadāru, see 14); sūrvā (disputed; perhaps mūrvā, Marsdenia tenacissima); bhṛta: filled, borne

hindi: पिप्पली यानी पीपर, कत्तृण यानी एक घास, उशीर यानी खस, दारु यानी सम्भवतः देवदारु और सूर्वा से भरा जल।
english: Water filled with pippalī (long pepper), kattṛṇa (a grass, identity uncertain), uśīra (vetiver), dāru (probably devadāru) and sūrvā (identity disputed).
notes: GROUPING: continues in 21 (verb pibet). "bhṛta" (lit. "filled, borne") is rendered "filled with"; "prepared with, infused with" is the probable sense but is not stated. Identifications: pippalī = Piper longum (standard); kattṛṇa = a fragrant grass, perhaps rauhiṣa (Cymbopogon), disputed; uśīra = Vetiveria zizanioides (standard); sūrvā = mūrvā, Marsdenia tenacissima, disputed; the dāru as in unit 14. Printed "kattṛṇa" is kept.

words.gloss: sauvarcala (a salt, black salt; standard); mixed
kindling (dīpana; a stimulant of the digestive fire)

hindi: सौवर्चल यानी काले नमक से मिला, दीपन यानी अग्नि को प्रदीप्त करने वाला और हृदय में शोधन करने वाला जल पिए।
english: One should drink it mixed with sauvarcala (black salt), kindling (dīpana) and cleansing in the heart.
notes: Object "water" is carried from 20; the words dīpanam and hṛdiśodhanam are accusative singular neuter, read as agreeing with the water. Identification: sauvarcala = sochal or black salt (standard). "hṛdi-śodhana" is kept as "cleansing in the heart", the text gives no further detail.

words.gloss: vacā (sweet flag, Acorus calamus; standard); nāgara (dry ginger, Zingiber officinale; standard); śaṭhī (disputed; Hedychium spicatum or Curcuma zedoaria)
curd; maṇḍa (the watery or creamy part)

hindi: अथवा वचा यानी बच, नागर यानी सोंठ और शठी, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, दही के मण्ड से मिश्रित।
english: Or vacā (sweet flag), nāgara (dry ginger) and śaṭhī (identity disputed), mixed with curd-maṇḍa.
notes: GROUPING: continues 20-21, with 23 giving the vehicles (the sentence continues in 23). "mūrcchita" (lit. "swooned, thickened") is rendered "mixed" as a conjecture on the use for drugs; "prepared" is another possible sense. "dadhimaṇḍa" kept literal ("curd-maṇḍa"), the watery or creamy part of curd by standard use. Identifications: vacā = Acorus calamus (standard); nāgara = dry ginger (standard); śaṭhī = Hedychium spicatum or Curcuma zedoaria (disputed).

hindi: पीने योग्य हों, प्रसन्ना से, या अरिष्ट से अथवा आसव से।
english: They should be drunk with prasannā (a clear liquor), or with ariṣṭa or with āsava (fermented liquors).
notes: Completes 22. "prasannā" is read as the clear liquor (a kind of surā), the standard sense; "ariṣṭa" and "āsava" are two kinds of fermented liquor and are kept as terms.

words.gloss: palāśa (flame of the forest, Butea monosperma; standard)

hindi: पहला शब्द छपाई में बिगड़ा है और उसका अनुवाद नहीं किया गया; अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार पथ्या यानी हरड़, पलाश यानी ढाक, चित्रक यानी चीता और शठी।
english: The first word, printed dārutrikaṭuukam, is damaged and is not translated, on a conjectural reading; pathyā (chebulic myrobalan), palāśa (flame of the forest), citraka (leadwort) and śaṭhī.

text_flags.why: possible: damaged print, doubled u-sign; "trikaṭūṣaka" is only a guess (not adopted)

notes: GROUPING: 24 and 25 form one statement (verb pibet in 25, "having ground ... should drink"). The first word is damaged (doubled u-sign in the print, apparently "dāru-trikaṭu" plus a damaged ending); it is kept unsplit and no reading is built on it. Identifications: pathyā = Terminalia chebula (standard); palāśa = Butea monosperma (standard); citraka = Plumbago zeylanica (standard); śaṭhī as in 22 (disputed).

words.gloss: kuṣṭha (costus, Saussurea costus; a drug name; standard)

hindi: मूत्र के साथ पीसकर और कुष्ठ यानी कूठ को भी, पिए; और दीपन क्षारों को भी।
english: Having ground (them) with urine, and kuṣṭha (costus), one should drink; and the kindling (dīpana) kṣāras.
notes: Completes 24; the order "having ground ... and kuṣṭha ... with urine" is kept as printed (kuṣṭha is a drug name here, costus, Saussurea costus; standard). What is drunk (the ground drugs of 24 or the kṣāras) is not fully stated; "kṣāra" is kept as a term.

words.gloss: of the dāśamūla (the group of ten roots; standard group)

hindi: और इसके लिए मूत्र सहित दशमूल वाली बस्ति दे।
english: And one should administer to him a basti with urine, of the dāśamūla (the ten roots).
notes: The members of the dāśamūla group are not listed in the text and are not listed here. "vidadhyāt" is rendered "should administer" (OPEN item in the glossary, similar verbs).

hindi: प्रयुक्त और अल्प वीर्य वाला, दोषों से भरे में, रूक्ष में, अथवा क्रूर आशय वाले में।
english: Applied with little potency (vīrya), in one rich in doṣa, in a dry one, or in one with a harsh abode (āśaya).
notes: GROUPING: 27 and 28 form one statement (verb ruṇdhyāt in 28). The subject basti is supplied only in 28. "yukta" is read as "applied" and "alpavīrya" as "of little potency"; "krūrāśaya" is kept literal ("harsh abode"); compare "krūrakoṣṭha" in 35. "olpa" for "alpa" as in unit 6 (recorded there).

hindi: दोषों से ढकी हुई और रुके हुए मार्ग वाली बस्ति वायु को रोके।
english: The basti, covered by doṣa and with its path blocked, may obstruct the wind.

text_flags.why: possible: spurious n; "doṣāvṛta" fits the sense and parallels unit 36

notes: Two print problems: "doṣānvṛto" is read as doṣa-āvṛtaḥ (compare 36, "āvṛto doṣaiḥ"), the spurious n being a probable mis-print; "ruddhamārgoṃ" has a stray anusvara. "samīraṇa" is a name of the wind. The subject "the basti" is the same as in 27.

hindi: वह विपरीत मार्ग से गई वायु आध्मान और मर्म में पीड़ा करे।
english: That wind, gone the wrong way, would cause distension (ādhmāna) and oppression of the vital parts (marma).
notes: Continues 28. "savimārgo" is read as sa vimārgaḥ ("that, gone the wrong way"); the alternative "sa-vimārga" (with a wrong path) is possible. "marma" are the vital parts or points of the body; kept as a term.

hindi: गुदा और कोष्ठ में जलन तथा अण्डकोष और वंक्षण में वेदना।
english: Burning of the anus and koṣṭha (storehouse, belly), and pain in the testicles and groins.
notes: Elliptical: verb "kuryāt" of 29 is carried over, none is supplied. "gudakoṣṭha" may be read as the koṣṭha of the anus; "anus and koṣṭha" is taken. "muṣka" = testicle (also scrotum).

hindi: हृदय को शूलों से रोकता है और इधर-उधर दौड़ता है।
english: It obstructs the heart with pains, and runs here and there.
notes: The subject is not stated; the wind (anila) of 29 is understood, but it is only supplied as "it". "itaścetaśca" = itaḥ ca itaḥ ca, "here and there".

hindi: उसमें, जिसका शरीर भली-भाँति अभ्यक्त और स्वेदित है, वर्ति का प्रयोग करे।
english: In that case, to one whose body is well anointed and sweated, one should apply a varti (suppository).

text_flags.why: orthographic doubling of t; normalised in words

notes: The print writes "varttim" with doubled t, normalised to varti in words (recorded once). "varti" is kept as a term (a wick-shaped suppository). The unit says "of one whose body ..." (genitive) and "applies a varti"; the direction of application is not stated and is not added.

words.gloss: pīlu (toothbrush tree, Salvadora persica; probable); sarṣapa (mustard, Brassica juncea; probable); urine; having

hindi: और बिल्व आदि वाला निरूह पीलु यानी सम्भवतः जाल, सर्षप यानी सरसों और मूत्र वाला हो।
english: And the nirūha (a decoction enema) beginning with bilva should have pīlu (probably the toothbrush tree), sarṣapa (probably mustard) and urine.

text_flags.why: orthographic variant (v for b); normalised in words

notes: The print writes "vilva" for bilva (orthographic, normalised, recorded once). The members of the bilva group are not listed. "nirūha" is kept as a term (a decoction enema; standard). Identifications: pīlu = Salvadora persica (probable); sarṣapa = mustard, probably Brassica juncea (probable).

hindi: और अनुवासन, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार जिसका पहला भाग सरला है उस बिगड़े शब्द से सिद्ध किया हुआ।
english: And an anuvāsana (oil enema) prepared with the damaged word saralāmadaruibhyām, on a conjectural reading beginning with sarala.

text_flags.why: possible: damaged print; suggestion is a guess from the ending -bhyām and the usual pairing, not adopted

notes: The word "saralāmadaruibhyāṃ" is damaged in the print (a displaced i-sign); the ending -bhyām suggests an instrumental dual ("with the two"), and the beginning looks like saralā (sarala, chir pine, Pinus roxburghii, probable), but the rest is unclear and no reading is built on it; a possible original is "saralā-devadārubhyām" (with sarala and devadāru), a guess only. Printed word kept unsplit.

hindi: बहुत दोष और बल वाले में तथा क्रूर कोष्ठ वाले में बस्ति पतली और मृदु हो।
english: In one with much doṣa and strength, with a harsh koṣṭha (storehouse, belly), a basti thin and mild,

text_flags.why: possible: stray tilde in the print

notes: GROUPING: 35 and 36 form one statement (verb pratihanti in 36). The print has a tilde in "bahu~doṣabale", taken as a mis-print; the reading "much doṣa and strength" is kept but not secure (bala could also be "strong").

hindi: ठंडी, अल्प और दोषों से ढकी हुई वह वायु को रोकती है।
english: Cold, small and covered by the doṣas, it obstructs the wind.
notes: The subject is the basti of 35 ("it"). Print forms: "śīto'lpaścāvṛto" = śītaḥ alpaḥ ca āvṛtaḥ.

words.gram: pres. part. anu-√sṛ, m. nom. sg.

hindi: ऊपर की ओर शरीर में चलती हुई वह वायु सिर की पीड़ा करे।
english: That wind (vāyu), moving upward along the body, would cause head-pain (headache).
notes: Continues 36. Modern equivalent: śiroruj = headache (standard).

hindi: गर्दन की जकड़न, प्रतिश्याय यानी जुकाम, बहरापन और दृष्टि का भ्रम।
english: Stiffness of the neck, pratiśyāya (nasal catarrh), deafness and disturbance of vision.
notes: Elliptical: the verb "kuryāt" of 37 is carried over, none is supplied. Modern equivalents: pratiśyāya = coryza, nasal catarrh (standard); dṛṣṭivibhrama = disturbed or confused vision (standard).

words.gloss: hot; oil; salt; smeared; sweated; pressed, kneaded

hindi: उसे, जिस पर गर्म तेल और नमक लगाया गया है, जो स्वेदित और मर्दित है।
english: Him, smeared with hot oil and salt, sweated and kneaded.
notes: GROUPING: 39, 40 and 41 form one statement (verb yojayet in 41, object tam). "mardita" (lit. "ground, crushed") is rendered "kneaded"; massaged is also possible.

words.gloss: with pradhamana (blowing of powder into the nose)

hindi: तीक्ष्ण धूमों, प्रधमन, नस्य और आस्य-विरेचनों से।
english: With sharp smokes, with pradhamana (powder-blowing), nasya (nasal medicines), and mouth-purgings (āsyavirecana),
notes: Continues 39 (verb in 41). "dhūma" is smoke (inhaled smoke); "pradhamana" and "nasya" are kept as terms. "āsyavirecana" is kept literal ("mouth-evacuation"); what exactly is evacuated is not stated.

hindi: विरेचनों और बस्तियों से, जो अनुलोम गति वाले हैं, शीघ्र उसका उपचार करे।
english: With purgations and bastis, quickly, one should treat (him) with ānulomika (following the natural direction) (ones).
notes: Completes 39-40; the object "him" is carried from 39. "ānulomika" means "following the natural (downward) direction"; kept literal. Which of the preceding instrumentals it qualifies is not fixed by the grammar.
